As soon as she arrived in Vienna, Teona had no problem socializing, thanks to her naturally friendly persona. Although exchange students can join the Erasmus Buddy Network, which pairs them with a local student for guidance through the experience, she didn’t feel the need to apply.
“I just felt like I would find my own buddies within the university community, especially through the events organized by the Erasmus Student Network (ESN),” said Teona.

Two years can feel like a decade in business today, where time is ticking faster than ever. Maria Bozhilova (EMBA ’16) has learned this lesson very well. Owner and Director of Telecom Consulting Partners (TCP), a small consulting company that works with major global technology players, Maria has implemented AI across major touchpoints of her team’s work. Yet, she doesn’t give in to the technological blindness many leaders fall prey to, and instead adopts a very grounded, human-first approach.

A few years later, Maria tried again, this time with a different model. She founded Telecom Consulting Partners, and fiver years later, it keeps growing. The company partners with global technology vendors and helps translate their solutions into local markets and long-term commercial opportunities. After overcoming the initial challenges of establishing a business, Maria finds herself navigating a new reality. She is running her company in a world where technology has a seat on the table.
